angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 417,420 km at 41.80 pc = 0.13 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 23.9215 +/- 0.0099 mas (same row, RUWE 0.75): 41.80 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.6 +/- 0.02 solar radii from Giacalone et al. 2022, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-833 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163...99G/abstract): 417,420 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.61 +/- 0.03 solar masses from Giacalone et al. 2022, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-833 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163...99G/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3920 +/- 160 K from Giacalone et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-833 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163...99G/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Giacalone et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-833 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163...99G/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-833.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.667, rounded to two decimals
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-833 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -1.11104, from TICv8 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019AJ....158..138S/abstract)
projectedRotationSpeedSource: SIMBAD, BPM 5856: projected rotation speed 3.7 km/s, the measurement SIMBAD prefers (2006A&A...460..695T)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
